course: Computer Science — Programming, Data and Systems
attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
description: An introductory computer science course: computational thinking, programming fundamentals, data structures, algorithms, systems and networks, and the ethics of computing.

concepts.title: Algorithms and algorithmic thinking
concepts.summary: An algorithm is a finite, unambiguous sequence of steps, and writing one down is a separate skill from running it.

concepts.title: Decomposition and abstraction
concepts.summary: Breaking a problem into smaller pieces and hiding detail are the two moves most problem solving depends on.

concepts.title: Pattern recognition and generalisation
concepts.summary: Spotting that two problems share a structure lets one solution serve both.

concepts.title: Binary representation
concepts.summary: Computers store everything as bits, so numbers, text, images and sound are all encodings.

concepts.title: Number bases and conversion
concepts.summary: Binary, denary and hexadecimal are the same values written differently, and conversion is repeated division or grouping.

concepts.title: Representing text, images and sound
concepts.summary: Each medium has a standard encoding, and every encoding trades quality against size.

concepts.title: Boolean logic and truth tables
concepts.summary: AND, OR and NOT combine conditions, and a truth table enumerates every case.

concepts.title: Logic circuits
concepts.summary: Logic gates implement Boolean expressions in hardware, and any circuit can be described by a truth table.

concepts.title: Variables, types and assignment
concepts.summary: A variable is a named location holding a value of some type, and assignment replaces what was there.

concepts.title: Operators and expressions
concepts.summary: Arithmetic, comparison and logical operators combine values, and precedence decides the order.

concepts.title: Input, output and casting
concepts.summary: Reading input as text and converting it to the type you need is where most beginner bugs live.

concepts.title: Selection and conditional logic
concepts.summary: A condition chooses which block runs, and nesting conditions expresses compound decisions.

concepts.title: Iteration and loops
concepts.summary: A loop repeats work, and the three parts that matter are initialisation, condition and update.

concepts.title: Nested loops and pattern problems
concepts.summary: A loop inside a loop scales multiplicatively, which is both its power and its cost.

concepts.title: Functions and parameters
concepts.summary: A function names a reusable block, takes inputs and returns a result, which is how programs stay readable.

concepts.title: Scope and lifetime
concepts.summary: Where a name is visible and how long its value survives are decided by where it was declared.

concepts.title: Strings and string processing
concepts.summary: Text is a sequence of characters, so indexing, slicing and joining are the core operations.

concepts.title: Lists and arrays
concepts.summary: An indexed collection stores many values under one name and allows traversal and modification.

concepts.title: Iterating over collections
concepts.summary: Traversing a collection with a loop is the pattern behind searching, counting and transforming.

concepts.title: Dictionaries and key-value data
concepts.summary: A dictionary maps a key to a value, giving fast lookup by meaning rather than by position.

concepts.title: Sorting and searching in practice
concepts.summary: Using a built-in sort or search correctly is a different skill from implementing one.

concepts.title: Reading and writing files
concepts.summary: Programs outlive their own run only if they persist data, and files are the simplest persistence.

concepts.title: Records and structured data
concepts.summary: Grouping related fields into one record makes code express the domain rather than the storage.

concepts.title: Debugging and tracing
concepts.summary: Debugging is hypothesis testing: form a guess about the cause and design a check that would falsify it.

concepts.title: Testing and test cases
concepts.summary: Normal, boundary and invalid cases each catch a different class of defect.

concepts.title: Errors, exceptions and validation
concepts.summary: Distinguishing a syntax error, a runtime error and a logic error tells you where to look.

concepts.title: Readability and naming
concepts.summary: Code is read far more often than it is written, so naming and structure are functional requirements.

concepts.title: Recursion
concepts.summary: A function that calls itself needs a base case, and without one it never terminates.

concepts.title: Abstract data types
concepts.summary: An abstract data type is defined by its operations, not by how those operations are implemented.

concepts.title: Stacks
concepts.summary: A stack is last in first out, which is exactly what nested structure such as brackets and call frames needs.

concepts.title: Queues
concepts.summary: A queue is first in first out, which is what fair scheduling and breadth-first traversal need.

concepts.title: Linked lists
concepts.summary: Nodes pointing to nodes allow cheap insertion and removal but lose random access.

concepts.title: Trees and binary search trees
concepts.summary: A tree encodes hierarchy, and the search-tree ordering rule turns lookup into a sequence of comparisons.

concepts.title: Hash tables
concepts.summary: Hashing turns a key into an index, giving near-constant lookup at the cost of collisions.

concepts.title: Graphs and their representations
concepts.summary: Adjacency lists and matrices represent the same graph with different cost profiles.

concepts.title: Algorithm efficiency and Big-O
concepts.summary: Big-O describes how running time grows with input size, ignoring constants and hardware.

concepts.title: Linear and binary search
concepts.summary: Binary search is far faster but demands sorted input, which is the trade it makes.

concepts.title: Comparison sorting algorithms
concepts.summary: Bubble, insertion, merge and quick sort differ in average and worst-case behaviour, not just speed.

concepts.title: Graph traversal
concepts.summary: Depth-first and breadth-first traversal visit the same nodes in different orders for different purposes.

concepts.title: Shortest paths
concepts.summary: Dijkstra's algorithm grows a known-distance set outward, which is only correct for non-negative weights.

concepts.title: Divide and conquer
concepts.summary: Splitting a problem, solving the parts and combining the results is a pattern with a predictable cost.

concepts.title: Optimisation and greedy methods
concepts.summary: A greedy choice is fast and sometimes optimal, and knowing when it fails is the real skill.

concepts.title: The fetch-decode-execute cycle
concepts.summary: A processor repeatedly fetches an instruction, decodes it and executes it, which is all a CPU does.

concepts.title: Memory and storage hierarchy
concepts.summary: Registers, cache, RAM and disk trade speed against capacity and cost at every level.

concepts.title: The stored program concept
concepts.summary: Instructions and data live in the same memory, which is what makes a general-purpose computer possible.

concepts.title: Operating systems
concepts.summary: An operating system manages memory, processes, files and devices so programs need not each do it.

concepts.title: Compilers and interpreters
concepts.summary: A compiler translates the whole program before running it; an interpreter translates as it goes.

concepts.title: Networks and topologies
concepts.summary: Star, mesh and bus topologies differ in resilience and cost, and the choice follows from the requirement.

concepts.title: Protocols and layering
concepts.summary: Splitting communication into layers lets each layer be replaced without rewriting the others.

concepts.title: Packets and routing
concepts.summary: Data is split into packets that may take different routes and are reassembled at the destination.

concepts.title: Encryption and authentication
concepts.summary: Encryption protects confidentiality while authentication establishes who is on the other end, and they solve different problems.

concepts.title: Common attack classes
concepts.summary: Malware, phishing, injection and denial of service each exploit a different assumption.

concepts.title: Defensive practice
concepts.summary: Input validation, least privilege and patching remove whole classes of vulnerability rather than individual bugs.

concepts.title: Data, privacy and consent
concepts.summary: Personal data has value, and consent, minimisation and retention limits are the mechanisms that constrain its use.

concepts.title: Algorithmic bias and fairness
concepts.summary: A model trained on biased data reproduces that bias, and it can do so while appearing objective.

concepts.title: Intellectual property and licensing
concepts.summary: Copyright, patents and open licences grant different rights, and using work without checking is a real risk.

concepts.title: Environmental and social cost of computing
concepts.summary: Computation consumes energy and materials, and the cost is distributed unevenly.

concepts.title: Automation, work and responsibility
concepts.summary: Automating a decision does not move responsibility for it away from the people who deployed it.
